candidates.exact_span: The 4Q3 is 431.3 cubic feet per second (cfs) and the harmonic mean low flow used for human health calculations is 1108 cfs.
candidates.computation_change_reason: These receiving-water low-flow values feed dilution and human-health limit derivations; different interpretation of which flow statistic applies or its magnitude would change critical dilution and the selected enforceable TRC limit.

candidates.exact_span: To convert 4Q3 expressed in cfs to 4Q3 expressed as MGD, the constant 1.548 cfs/MGD is used. The 4Q3 is 278.6 MGD and the harmonic mean low flow is 715.8 MGD.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The conversion constant and resulting MGD flows determine Qa in the critical-dilution calculation; a different conversion or flow value would change CD and therefore which TRC standard is selected as the permit limit.

candidates.exact_span: The NMWQS for total residual chlorine (TRC) are 11 ug/l for chronic and 19 ug/l for acute conditions.
candidates.computation_change_reason: These numeric water-quality standards are inputs to the stringency comparison that selects the enforceable end-of-pipe TRC limit; interpreting chronic versus acute applicability differently would change the applicable numeric limit.

candidates.exact_span: The NNWQS for TRC are 4000 ug/L for domestic water supply, and primary/secondary human contact; 19 ug/L for aquatic & wildlife habitat-acute; and, 11 ug/L for aquatic & wildlife habitat-chronic and livestock watering.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The permit selects the most stringent WQS from among these standards; different interpretation of which use classes apply or which numeric values bind would change the computed permit limit.

candidates.exact_span: Since acute conditions do not allow dilution; the limit must be met at end-of-pipe but chronic standards do allow dilution, the permit shall use the most stringent WQS for the permit limit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This establishes whether dilution may be credited and whether compliance is judged at end-of-pipe versus in-stream; a different reading would change the limit derivation method and the resulting enforceable numeric limit.

candidates.exact_span:
Qe = facility effluent or design flow; 6.67 MGD
Qa = 4Q3; 278.6 MGD
F = fraction of stream allowed for mixing; 1.0
candidates.computation_change_reason: These parameters define the critical-dilution denominator; different interpretation of effluent flow, receiving flow, or mixing fraction would change CD and the downstream limit-selection outcome.

candidates.exact_span:
The in-stream TRC concentration after allowing for dilution is; 11 ug/l ÷ 0.0234 = 470 ug/l.
Since this value is greater than the 19 ug/l end-of-pipe acute standard, the 19 ug/l is more
stringent and will be more protective.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This comparison logic determines which numeric standard governs; if the dilution-adjusted chronic value or the stringency test were interpreted differently, the selected enforceable limit could change.

candidates.exact_span:
The draft permit maintains the 19 ug/l end-of-pipe acute
limit since it is more stringent and will be more protective than the 11 ug/l dilution based chronic
limit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This nominates the operative numeric discharge limit for TRC; whether this 19 ug/l acute end-of-pipe limit is treated as the binding enforceable limit directly changes exceedance determinations for reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: the narrative limit for total residual chlorine shall be “No Measurable.”
candidates.computation_change_reason: This establishes a separate non-numeric effluent limitation alongside the 19 ug/l value; interpreting whether the narrative or numeric limit governs, or how 'No Measurable' is evaluated against reported results, would change limit-applicability and missing-evidence classification.

candidates.exact_span:
After dechlorination and prior to final disposal, the effluent shall contain NO
MEASURABLE (TRC) at any time.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The timing and process conditions define when the limitation and monitoring obligations attach; different interpretation of 'after dechlorination,' 'prior to final disposal,' or 'at any time' would change which periods require comparison to limits, which monitoring is required, and how absent or non-detect results are classified.

candidates.exact_span:
NO MEASURABLE will be defined as no detectable
concentration of TRC as determined by any approved method established in 40 CFR Part 136.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The approved-method and detection-limit definition determines what counts as a measurable exceedance versus a compliant non-detect; different interpretation would change numeric compliance comparisons and the semantics of missing or below-detection evidence.

candidates.exact_span: The effluent limitation for TRC is the instantaneous maximum and cannot be averaged for reporting purposes.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This prescribes that compliance must be judged on an instantaneous maximum basis rather than an average; interpreting the averaging prohibition differently would change whether reported measurements are compared correctly to the limit.

candidates.exact_span: The maximum dechlorinated TRC shall be monitored daily by grab sample.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This states a frequency and sample-type monitoring obligation; different interpretation of 'daily,' 'maximum dechlorinated TRC,' or 'grab sample' would change whether monitoring was required for evaluated periods.

candidates.exact_span: TRC shall be measured within fifteen (15) minutes of sampling.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This imposes a methodological timing requirement on valid monitoring; different interpretation of whether late analysis invalidates a result would change monitoring-obligation fulfillment and whether absent or questionable data constitute adequate evidence.
